Dynamo-lite — Distributed Key-Value Store

Distributed Systems ProjectTeam of 1

Ahmedabad University

Systems & Distributed Computing

Built a fault-tolerant distributed key-value store from scratch in Java, inspired by Amazon's Dynamo paper (SOSP 2007). Implemented consistent hashing with 150 virtual nodes per physical node for uniform key distribution, quorum-based replication (N=3, W=2, R=2) with parallel fanout across a real 3-node LAN cluster, and heartbeat-based failure detection. No frameworks or external libraries — raw TCP sockets, custom wire protocol, and hand-written request parser.

Key Outcomes:

System sustains reads and writes with 1-of-3 nodes down via quorum replication; auto-recovers missed writes through hinted handoff with under 5-second failure detection.

Technologies Used:

Java
Distributed Systems
Consistent Hashing
Quorum Replication
TCP Sockets
Multithreading
ConcurrentHashMap
ExecutorService
Swing

Planetary Exploration Rover: Hybrid AI Architecture

Oct 2025 - Dec 2025Team of 2

Ahmedabad University

Algorithms & AI

Developed a hybrid reactive-deliberative AI system for a Martian rover navigation. The system integrates a Reflex Agent for immediate hazard response (cliffs, traps, radiation) with an A* Deliberative Planner for long-term goal optimization. It features a complex battery management logic and a memory system to prevent hazard loops in a probabilistic 2D grid world.

Key Outcomes:

Achieved significant success rate improvement using Chebyshev heuristics; implemented a three-tier battery management system and conducted exhaustive statistical analysis across 30 epochs.

Technologies Used:

Python
A* Search
Heuristic Analysis
Hybrid Architectures

Five-Cycle Non-Pipelined RISC Processor (25-bit)

Feb 2025 - Apr 2025Team of 4

Ahmedabad University

Hardware Design

Implemented a 25-bit RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) processor in Verilog HDL, based on a five-stage non-pipelined architecture. This design adheres to the RISC philosophy for faster execution and greater hardware efficiency. The project involved designing key modules like the Instruction Fetch, Instruction Decode, Execute, Memory Access, and Write Back stages, including ALU, Control, and Output Logic, all successfully integrated for full functionality.

Key Outcomes:

Successfully designed and integrated 25-bit RISC processor modules (ALU, Control, Output Logic) in Verilog, demonstrating advanced computer architecture and HDL proficiency.
